title: EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE: reading the plan instead of guessing

videos.script: A query is slow, and three people have three theories. One blames the index, one blames the join, one blames the server. {{theories}} None of them has to guess. PostgreSQL will tell you what it decided to do, step by step, before it does it. {{explain}} That decision is the plan. It is a tree of small steps, and every step carries the planner's prediction: what it will cost, and how many rows will come out. {{tree}} Add one word, ANALYZE, and the server runs the query and writes down what really happened beside what it predicted. {{analyze}} Add another, BUFFERS, and every step says how many pages it touched, and whether they were already in memory. {{buffers}} This lesson is about reading all of that without getting lost. You read the tree from the inside out. You multiply by loops before you believe a number. You run anything that writes inside a transaction you roll back. {{rules}} And at the end you do the planner's arithmetic yourself, for one table, with a pencil. Two numbers from the catalogue, two settings, one multiplication each. {{pencil}} Once the cost stops being a mystery, the plan stops being one too. Lessons 4 to 7 read every plan this way. {{close}}
